papers.title: Cross-Sectional and Time-Series Tests of Return Predictability: Cross-Asset Momentum Approach
Cross-Sectional and Time-Series Momentum Returns and Market Dynamics: Evidence from Japan
papers.authors: Muhammad A. Cheema, Gilbert Nartea, Kenneth R. Szulczyk
papers.abstract: We test the behavioural theories of overconfidence and underreaction on cross-sectional (CS) and times-series (TS) momentum returns in the Japanese stock markets. Both CS and TS momentum returns are large and significant when the market continues in the same state and turns into losses when the market transitions to another state, consistent with the overconfidence but not the underreaction model. We find that TS conditional momentum returns exceed conditional CS momentum returns because of its active position since TS takes a net long (short) position following UP (DN) markets while CS is a zero-cost strategy irrespective of the market state. Finally, we find no relation between idiosyncratic volatility and momentum returns which is not supportive of either the overconfidence or underreaction model but implies that idiosyncratic volatility is not a significant limit to arbitrage in Japan.

papers.title: Cross-Sectional and Time-Series Momentum Returns and Market States
papers.authors: Muhammad A. Cheema, Gilbert V. Nartea, Yimei Man

papers.title: When Gradient Boosting Does Not Beat Momentum: A Significance-Tested, Walk-Forward Negative Result on Cross-Sectional Stock Selection in the Nifty 500
papers.abstract: A large literature reports that machine-learning models improve cross-sectional equity return prediction, mostly on deep, liquid U.S. markets and mostly as positive results. We ask one narrow, falsifiable question on the Indian Nifty 500 (2018-2026): does a gradient-boosted crosssectional ranker, trained on standard point-in-time features, beat a plain 12-1 momentum baseline when both are evaluated through the identical walk-forward protocol, transaction-cost model, and selection machinery? The momentum baseline is numerically ahead on every metric (outof-sample Sharpe 1.73 vs. 1.55, CAGR 41.7% vs. 38.8%), but the honest finding is stronger and quieter than "momentum wins." A stationary block bootstrap and a Jobson-Korkie-Memmel test both show the Sharpe difference is statistically indistinguishable from zero (95% CI [-0.31, +0.69]; bootstrap p = 0.47; JKM p = 0.37), and the ranker's information coefficient-the rank correlation between its predicted scores and realised forward returns-is indistinguishable from zero across 51 rebalances (mean-0.004, t =-0.22). In other words, the pre-specified regressor demonstrates no cross-sectional ranking skill; its returns track the baseline (correlation 0.90) only because it is fed momentum features and ends up holding near-identical baskets, and it underperforms in later folds. A native learning-to-rank objective recovers marginal skill and matches the baseline's Sharpe, but only by trading 1.8× as much, so it too fails to beat it. The added complexity, turnover, and opacity buy no distinguishable benefit, so parsimony selects the incumbent. We interpret this not as "ML does not work," but as a worked instance of the evaluation discipline-significance testing included-that any candidate signal must survive before it is believed. Harness, features, and figure data are released.

papers.title: Generative AI for European Asset Pricing: Alleviating the Momentum Anomaly
papers.abstract: We challenge the notion of classical factor models that concentrated factors, particularly the anomalous momentum factor, dominate the European stock market. We use a generative AI asset pricing model that incorporates the economic rationale of no-arbitrage and treats the European capital market as a complex system. This model outperforms all European benchmarks over 16 years out-of-sample with an annualized Sharpe ratio of 3.68, a cross-sectional R2 of over 22%, and an explained variation of over 13%. Using interpretable AI techniques, we find that the model sees a zoo of factors in the European market rather than just a concentrated set. Excellent results stem from time-conditional modeling, which requires momentum, especially for the tangency portfolio weights. Conditional betas can substitute momentum more efficiently. Overall, the risk-sharing mechanism for European assets is more complex than previously thought.

papers.title: Momentum Anomaly: Research In BIST100 Index
Cross-Asset Style Momentum
papers.abstract: This paper reports significant momentum profits among style portfolios of multiple asset classes. Previous studies have demonstrated style momentum within equity markets. The findings of this paper show that style momentum is not merely an equity market phenomenon, but a cross-asset phenomenon. A decomposition of profits reveals that profits are mostly attributable to positive auto-correlations of style returns. We interpret this result as being more consistent with the underreaction models than with the excess comovement and performance chasing models.

papers.title: "Beat the Market" Revisited An Independent Replication and Statistical Audit of an Intraday Momentum Strategy
papers.abstract: Zarattini, Aziz, and Barbon report that a simple intraday time-series momentum strategy applied to SPY produced a total return of 1,985%, an annualized return of 19.6%, and a Sharpe Ratio of 1.33 from May 2007 through April 2024. This paper performs an independent replication and a post-publication extension using approximately 2.6 million one-minute SPY observations from TradeStation spanning January 2000 through August 2026. After reconciling two material implementation details against the authors’ published Python reference code—the use of typical-price Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) and VWAP confirmation at entry—the original result is reproduced almost exactly: 1,989% total return and a Sharpe Ratio of 1.317 on the paper window under the closest paper-matching convention. The independent update also closely reproduces the authors’ September 2025 FAQ update: 2024 returns are 31.8% versus their 32.2%, and January–August 2025 returns are 1.4% versus their 1.0%. The longer sample changes the interpretation, but not in the simple form suggested by the pooled May 2024–August 2026 Sharpe of 0.35. Disaggregating the post-publication path reveals two sharply different regimes. Under a Q24-comparable monthly convention, May 2024–29 August 2025 returns 19.3% with Sharpe 1.057; using the exact first trading day after the 10 May 2024 publication, the corresponding return is 23.3% with Sharpe 1.284. By contrast, the subsequent 2 September 2025–14 August 2026 stretch returns -8.1% with Sharpe -0.461. Thus the evidence does not support a narrative of immediate post-publication alpha decay; it supports a strong initial post-publication period followed by a materially weak recent regime. A systematic search then evaluates asymmetric short filters, relative-volume sizing, volatility overlays, persistence filters, profit locks, breakeven rules, trade caps, daily loss limits, VWAP-dominance rules, intraday decay, regime overlays, and performance-based overlays. Only a small subset survives the consistent multi-window standard applied during the extension stage. The final frozen selected specification reaches a valid-period Sharpe Ratio of 1.274, a -14.8% maximum drawdown, and a 2110.6% total return over 2000–2026, while deliberately sacrificing terminal wealth relative to the baseline. To address multiple testing, a research ledger of 129 trials is reconstructed and 80 SPY search alternatives are identified. Combinatorially Symmetric Cross-Validation yields a Probability of Backtest Overfitting of 38.49% under the historical convention and 40.87% on a common-valid sample. The Deflated Sharpe Ratio of the final candidate, using 𝑁 = 80 as the primary multiple-testing count, is 99.999986796%. These statistics support a strong retrospective edge but do not provide a genuine prospective validation because the search was adaptive and the 2024–2026 data were observed during model development. The correct next experiment is therefore not another retrospective optimization, but the passage of time with frozen parameters.

papers.title: Out-of-Sample Evaluation of an Intraday Momentum Strategy for the S&P 500 ETF (SPY)
papers.abstract: Zarattini, Aziz, and Barbon (2025) present an intraday momentum strategy for SPY that achieves an annualized return of 19.6% and a Sharpe Ratio of 1.33 over the period 2007-2024. This paper independently replicates their strategy using IQFeed 1-minute data and evaluates its performance on approximately two years of out-of-sample data (May 2024 to March 2026). Our in-sample replication closely matches the original results, confirming the reproducibility of the strategy (Sharpe Ratio 1.34 over 2015-2024). However, out-of-sample performance deteriorates substantially: the strategy achieves a total return of only 9.4% versus 29.5% for a passive buy-and-hold, with a Sharpe Ratio of 0.39. The decline in risk-adjusted returns is statistically significant. We examine potential explanations for this degradation, including changing market microstructure, the proliferation of zero-days-to-expiration (0-DTE) options, and the possibility that the observed underperformance falls within historical drawdown norms. Our findings highlight the importance of out-of-sample validation for intraday trading strategies and contribute to the ongoing discussion about the persistence of momentum anomalies at high frequencies.

papers.title: Beat the Market An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY)
papers.authors: Carlo Zarattini, Andrew Aziz, Andrea Barbon
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the profitability of a simple, yet effective intraday momentum strategy applied to SPY, one of the most liquid ETFs that tracks the S&P 500. Unlike the academic literature that typically limits trading to the last 30 minutes of the trading session, our model initiates trend-following positions as soon as there is an indication of abnormal demand/supply imbalance in the intraday price action. Building on trading techniques commonly used by active day traders, which have been discussed in our previous papers, we introduce the use of dynamic trailing stops to mitigate downside risks while allowing for unlimited upside potential. From 2007 to early 2024, the resulting intraday momentum portfolio achieved a total return of 1,985% (net of costs), an annualized return of 19.6%, and a Sharpe Ratio of 1.33. We conduct extensive statistical tests to examine whether the profitability of the strategy is affected by different market volatility regimes and whether the estimated gamma imbalance of dealers could predict changes in strategy profitability. We analyze the daily profitability of the intraday momentum strategy with respect to day-of-the-week effects. Additionally, we evaluate its performance against well-known technical daily patterns to understand its behavior under various market conditions. Given the short-term nature of the model, we also assess the impact of commissions and slippage on the overall profitability of the strategy.

papers.title: Noise-band Intraday Momentum in Nasdaq-100 Futures
papers.abstract: This paper adapts the intraday momentum strategy of Zarattini et al. (2024), which trades breaks from a "noise area" around the open on the SPY ETF, to Nasdaq-100 futures (NQ) at a fixed size of one micro contract and under constraints that permit unattended webhook execution. On one-minute data from 2020 to July 2026 the executable rule earns +$10.26 per trading day net of costs (day-block bootstrap 95% interval [+$3.27, +$17.25]), with a daily Sharpe ratio of 1.14 and positive results in each of seven calendar years, two of them only marginally. The paper reports the degradation at each step from the published specification to the executable one, a lookahead audit of the trailing stop, and execution stress tests showing that one index point of slippage on stop fills removes 22% of the edge. A three-year block bootstrap of drawdown gives a 95th-percentile maximum drawdown of $3,406 as backtested and $4,081 under combined lag and slippage, which determines the minimum account size for deployment. The rule is one of two survivors among 144 preregistered tests on the same archive, all intervals are in-sample, and no live contract has been traded. Pre-registered thresholds for the forward test are stated.

papers.title: Market Intraday Momentum in Japan: Evidence from the Nikkei Stock Index
Intraday Option Return: A Tale of Two Momentum
papers.authors: Zhi Da, Ruslan Goyenko, Chengyu Zhang

papers.title: Improvements to Intraday Momentum Strategies Using Parameter Optimization and Different Exit Strategies
Intraday Momentum in FX Markets: Disentangling Informed Trading from Liquidity Provision
papers.authors: Gert Elaut, Michael Frömmel, Kevin Lampaert
papers.abstract: We examine intraday momentum in the RUB-USD exchange market and its relationship with informed trading and liquidity provision. Using tick-by-tick transaction level data from the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX) for the period 2005 to 2014, we establish the presence of intraday momentum, defined as a significantly positive relationship between the first half-hour return and the last-half hour return. We find that, for our specific dataset, intraday momentum does not appear to be the result of informed trading. Instead, our results suggest that intraday momentum is consistent with risk-aversion for overnight holdings among liquidity providers.

papers.title: Stock’s Macro Announcement Incremental Information and Intraday Momentum
papers.authors: Xiang Zhang, Ke Zhang, Yulu Li, Zhiyuan Pan

papers.title: Intraday Momentum: Evidence from the Crude Oil Market
papers.authors: Zhuzhu Wen, Ro Cho, Diandian Ma, Yahua Xu
papers.abstract: Our analysis of high-frequency United States Oil Fund (USO) data from 2006 to 2018 shows that intraday momentum exists in the crude oil market. The first half-hour return from the previous day’s market close positively predicts the last half-hour return both in-sample and out-of-sample. Predictability is stronger during crisis periods and on days with higher realized volatility, higher trading volume, higher overnight returns, and jumps. A market timing strategy, constructed by using the first half-hour return as a timing signal, outperforms two other benchmark strategies.

papers.title: Intraday Time Series Momentum: Global Evidence and Links to Market Characteristics
papers.authors: Zeming Li, Athanasios Sakkas, Andrew Urquhart
papers.abstract: This paper studies intraday time-series momentum (ITSM) in an international setting by employing high-frequency data of 16 developed markets. We show that ITSM is economically sizable and statistically significant both in- and out-of-sample in most countries. Based on existing theories of investor behavior, we propose and test four hypotheses to reveal the source of ITSM profitability. We document both in the cross-section and time-series dimension that ITSM is stronger when liquidity is low, volatility is high and new information is discrete. Overall, our analysis suggests that the ITSM is driven by both market microstructure and behavioral factors.

papers.title: Intraday Momentum in Chinese Commodity Futures Markets
papers.authors: Wei Zhang, Pengfei Wang, Yi Li

papers.title: Intraday Return Predictability in the Cryptocurrency Markets: Momentum, Reversal, or Both
papers.authors: Zhuzhu Wen, Elie Bouri, Yahua Xu, Yang Zhao
papers.abstract: This paper reports evidence of intraday return predictability, consisting of both intraday momentum and reversal, in the cryptocurrency market. Using high-frequency price data on Bitcoin from March 3, 2013, to May 31, 2020, it shows that the patterns of intraday return predictability change in the presence of large intraday price jumps, FOMC announcement release, liquidity levels, and the outbreak of the COVID-19. Intraday return predictability is also found in other actively traded cryptocurrencies such as Ethereum, Litecoin, and Ripple. Further analysis shows that the timing strategy based on the intraday predictors produces higher economic value than the benchmark strategy such as the always-long or the buy-and-hold. Evidence of intraday momentum can be explained in light of the theory of late-informed investors, whereas evidence of intraday reversal, which is unique to the cryptocurrency market, can be related to investors’ overreaction to non-fundamental information and overconfidence bias.

papers.title: Delta-Hedging Demand and Intraday Momentum: Evidence from China
Intraday Momentum and Return Predictability: Evidence from the Crude Oil Market
papers.authors: Zhuzhu Wen, Xu Gong, Diandian Ma, Yahua Xu
papers.abstract: Intraday return predictability has firstly been identified in the equity markets, and we extend the analysis to the crude oil market by using high-frequency United States Oil Fund data from 2006 to 2018. We find a different intraday prediction pattern in the oil market, where only the first half-hour returns positively predict the last half-hour returns. A market timing strategy based on the findings generates substantial profits. We further decompose the first half-hour return into the overnight and the open half-hour components, and find that the former contains more predictive information. Economic mechanisms of the infrequent portfolio rebalancing and the presence of late-informed investors explain our findings. Notably, unlike equity markets, the oil market exhibits a unique intraday trading volume pattern, caused by the release of two routine oil inventory announcements. However, the information contained in the inventory announcements does not offer predictability to the last half-hour returns.

papers.title: Is There an Intraday Momentum Effect in Commodity Futures and Options: Evidence from the Chinese Market
Modeling Intraday Momentum and Reversal by a Parsimonious Diffusion Process
papers.authors: Shiqing Ling, Zhenya Liu, Shixuan Wang

papers.title: Intraday Momentum in Spot FX and Currency Futures: Signal Persistence, the JPY Amplification Mechanism, and the Cost Barrier to Retail Exploitability
papers.abstract: We test the intraday momentum effect documented by Gao et al. (2018) and Baltussen et al. (2021) across five spot FX CFD instruments and one currency futures contract. Using M5 Dukascopy data for spot pairs (2012–2024) and M1 Databento data for 6J CME futures (2019–2024), with a strict in-sample/out-of-sample split (IS: 2012–2018; OOS: 2019–2024), we document three principal findings. First, the London Open 30-minute sign signal is statistically significant on five of six instruments in both periods (permutation p < 0.001), with GBPUSD exhibiting a reversed signal direction consistent with the absence of JPY carry-trade amplification, confirming that the intraday momentum mechanism extends to retail market structures. Second, we identify a JPY Amplification Mechanism: JPY-denominated instruments exhibit regression coefficients approximately 3.8× larger than non-JPY pairs (average OOS β: 0.000859 vs. 0.000226), with GBPUSD treated separately due to its structurally reversed signal direction, consistent with the structural role of JPY as a global risk-sentiment amplifier and carry-trade funding currency. Third, after applying realistic round-trip transaction costs from actual platform data, USDJPY spot is the sole instrument producing a positive cost-adjusted edge (OOS Sortino: +0.748), while four spot pairs and 6J futures fail to clear their respective cost hurdles when standard prop-firm position sizing constraints are applied. A direct spot-futures comparison reveals a mechanistically important divergence in 2022: while BOJ Yield Curve Control interventions destroyed the spot signal, 6J futures maintained positive performance (annual Sharpe: +0.383 vs. −0.557), indicating that futures microstructure partially insulates the signal from central bank intervention. Regime filter tests confirm the USDJPY baseline is filter-robust. These results establish that the intraday momentum mechanism is pervasive across retail FX instruments but faces a steep cost barrier, with JPY carry dynamics as the primary exploitable source of intraday directional information.

papers.title: Time Series Momentum and Reversal: Intraday Information from Realized Semivariance
papers.authors: Zhenya Liu, Shanglin Lu, Bo Li, Shixuan Wang

papers.title: Observable and Latent Regime Structure in Intraday Gap Reversals: A Taxonomy of Strategy-Level Regime Dependence
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a taxonomy of regime dependence in trading strategies, distinguishing between observable-regime strategies, where the conditioning variable is known at trade entry, and latent-regime strategies, where the relevant regime must be inferred from outcome history. The distinction has a precise statistical consequence: observable-regime strategies produce conditionally i.i.d. trade outcomes (no autocorrelation), while latent-regime strategies produce autocorrelated outcomes (exploitable by performance filters). Using intraday gap-reversal strategies on daily FX bars as the empirical setting, I demonstrate the taxonomy by decomposing gaps relative to a macro trend indicator into two structurally distinct populations. Gaps opposing the prevailing trend represent responsive market activity and exhibit strong mean-reversion (profit factor 1.59, 17,716 trades, 26 years of out-of-sample data, zero losing years). Gaps aligned with the 1 Observable and Latent Regime Structure trend represent initiative activity and do not revert (profit factor 0.74). The observable regime variable (trend direction at entry) fully accounts for the performance difference: within each subpopulation, outcomes are i.i.d. with no residual autocorrelation, confirming that the strategy's edge derives from correct regime classification rather than from temporal persistence. Crossmarket replication on a European equity index confirms the decomposition at the daily timeframe. The taxonomy provides a theoretical framework for understanding when performance filters (such as Markov regime models) add value and when they are unnecessary.

papers.title: The Lazy Man's Momentum Strategy
An Intraday Trend-Following Trading Strategy on Equity Derivatives in India
Value & Estrategia De Momentum, ¿Tiene Sentido? (Value & Momentum Strategy, Does It Make Sense?)
papers.abstract: Spanish Abstract: En este paper examinamos el comportamiento de porfolios basados en estrategias cuantitativas orientados tanto al Value Investment como Momentum. Además, encontramos que combinando ambos enfoques clasificando el universo de valores, tanto en Europa como en EEUU, dentro del ranking de Value con Momentum obtenemos retornos constantes y anormalmente mayores. Basamos nuestro trabajo en el trabajo previo de Wesley Gray y Jack Vogel para ilustrar nuestros estudios y completar nuevas evidencias. Proporcionamos un método de screening que cumple con los criterios y casos de estudio revisados en el paper. English Abstract: This paper examines the performance of portfolios based on quantitative strategies both Value Investing and Momentum. Besides we find that combining both approaches by ranking the universe of securities, both in Europe and EEUU, within Value ranking on Momentum we get constant returns and abnormally bigger. We base our paper on Wesley Gray and Jack Vogel previous work to illustrate our studies as well as completing new evidences. We provide a screening method that meets the criteria and case studies reviewed in the paper.

papers.title: Momentum - Reversal Strategy
papers.abstract: Various theories have been presented to explain momentum and reversals in stock returns. Based on the model of Hong and Stein (1999), this paper creates a hybrid strategy to avoid the losses from the reversal phase. The risk-adjusted returns of the new strategy are significantly higher than those of the traditional momentum strategy. Moreover, the risk-adjusted returns of the new strategy cannot be fully explained by Carhart’s four-factor model. Such a finding is robust in different time periods and size quintiles. Overall, this paper exploits the interaction between heterogeneous investors and generates distinctive applications.

papers.title: A Dynamic Price Jump Exit and Re-Entry Strategy for Intraday Trading Algorithms Based on Market Volatility
papers.authors: Dirk Johan Coetzee Koegelenberg, Jan  Harm van Vuuren
papers.abstract: Trading algorithms adopt automated risk management systems in order to mitigate against market risk and extreme market events. These systems are aimed at reducing potential losses due to unforeseen market events caused by a plethora of extraneous factors. One such unforeseen event is a price jump, a vaguely defined but abrupt change in asset price. In this paper we propose a novel exit and re-entry strategy (suitable for intraday trading algorithms) capable of identifying market exit points, triggered by price jumps, and thereafter monitoring market stability conditions until an appropriate point of market re-entry has been identified. Validation results indicate that the proposed exit and re-entry strategy provides a new perspective on identifying points/intervals of price jump when compared with existing price jump identification methods and the opinion of a subject matter expert.

papers.title: Multi-Asset A/A+ Momentum Fair Value Gap Strategy
papers.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous quantitative analysis of the Multi-Asset A/A+ Momentum Fair Value Gap (FVG) Trading Strategy, backtested across Gold (XAUUSD), Euro (EURUSD), British Pound (GBPUSD), and Japanese Yen (USDJPY) over the calendar year 2025, using one-minute OHLC data from HistData. The strategy employs strict multi-confluence filtering: momentum leg detection on the 5-minute timeframe, Fair Value Gap identification within a 2-hour forward window, and Higher Timeframe (1H) structural confluence via EMA-20, EMA-50, and a 30-period Point of Control. Setups are classified as A-grade or A+-grade based on body ratio thresholds and HTF alignment quality. Over 473 qualifying trades, the strategy produced +265.0 R in cumulative profit-equivalent to a $66,250 net gain on a $50,000 account risking $250 per trade-representing a 132.5% annual return. The overall win rate was 78.0%, with A+-grade setups achieving 86.7%. Maximum drawdown was contained to-$1,000 (-2.0%), demonstrating exceptional capital preservation alongside strong absolute performance.

papers.title: Evaluating a 12-1 Month Momentum Strategy (2005-2024)
Refining ETF Asset Momentum Strategy
When Does Risk-Managed Momentum Add Value? An Out-of-Sample, Regime-Conditional, and Statistically Tested Study of a Volatility-Targeted Dual-Momentum Strategy
papers.abstract: A defensive strategy is expected to trail passive equities across a sustained bull market, so "did it beat the market?" is the wrong question. This paper asks a conditional one: under what market conditions does risk-managed allocation add value, and are the differences statistically distinguishable from noise? I build a rules-based backtest combining dual-momentum asset selection with volatility targeting across four asset classes (Feb 2013–Jun 2026), correcting common backtest errors (lookahead bias, turnover-based transaction costs, a real time-varying risk-free rate), and subject it to out-of-sample and walk-forward validation, regime-conditional analysis, a 36-configuration sensitivity grid, and block-bootstrap significance tests. The results are instructive because they are mixed: the strategy reduces volatility and drawdown versus buy-and-hold but does not outperform a 60/40 benchmark in any configuration, and its full-sample risk-reduction benefits are not statistically significant. Its value is regime-dependent, strong in the slow 2022 bear market, worst in the fast COVID crash. Walk-forward re-optimization degrades out-of-sample performance, an empirical demonstration of the backtest-overfitting trap. An engineered daily crash-guard overlay delivers statistically significant downside protection but exposes a fundamental crash-protection-versus-whipsaw tradeoff. All results are reproducible from cached data and a fixed seed. Code, data, and interactive demo: github.com/aarivgoyal/quant-momentum-risk-targeting (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21444647).

papers.title: Intraday Price Asymmetry and Next-Day Intraday Returns in the S&P 500
papers.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between intraday price asymmetry and next-day intraday returns in U.S. equity markets. It introduces a simple, range-based measure of intraday asymmetry constructed from daily open, high, and low prices to capture directional imbalances in intraday price movements relative to the opening level. Using more than two decades of data for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the analysis documents a contrarian relationship between intraday asymmetry and subsequent intraday performance. Trading sessions characterized by negative intraday asymmetry are followed, on average, by stronger next-day intraday returns, while positive asymmetry is associated with weaker subsequent intraday performance, despite the long-run upward bias of equity markets. Conditional long and short exposures derived from the measure exhibit economically meaningful return patterns, with evidence of conditional return variation on the short side concentrated during periods of elevated volatility and market stress. The analysis is intentionally descriptive and does not rely on assumptions about order flow, trading volume, or specific microstructure mechanisms. The results are consistent with temporary price pressure and inventory-related dynamics rather than persistent intraday trends, highlighting information contained in the intraday price path that is not captured by standard return-based measures.

papers.title: Overnight Anomaly
papers.abstract: There are a lot of day traders in the market which decide their trading strategy when the market opens. However, as we all know, to be successful, we have to be different from the market. The following is a short research into the performance of day trading versus overnight trading strategy.

papers.title: Market Sentiment and an Overnight Anomaly
papers.abstract:
Various research shows that market sentiment, also called investor sentiment, plays a role in market returns. Market sentiment refers to the general mood on the financial markets and investors' overall tendency to trade. The mood on the market is divided into two main types, bullish and bearish. Naturally, rising prices indicate bullish sentiment. On the other hand, falling prices indicate bearish sentiment. This paper shows various ways to measure market sentiment and its influence on returns.

Additionally, we take a look at an overnight anomaly in combination with three market sentiment indicators. We analyse the Brain Market sentiment indicator in addition to VIX and the short-term trend in SPY ETF. Our aim is not to build a trading system. Instead, it is to analyse financial markets behaviour. Overall the transaction costs of this kind of strategy would be very high. However, more appropriate than using this system on its own would be to use it as an overlay when deciding when to make trades.

papers.title: Overnight Return Momentum and the Timing of Trading Volume
ATS-Mediated Erosion of the Overnight Reversal Anomaly: Evidence from Korea's NXT Launch
papers.abstract:
We exploit Korea's March 2025 launch of NXT---the first independent alternative trading system (ATS) to produce premarket prices outside the KRX consolidated tape---as a natural experiment for the structural decay
of the overnight reversal anomaly. Using a daily panel of Korean common stocks from 2015 to 2026, we document that a strategy buying stocks with extreme negative overnight returns at the open and selling
them at the close earns a mean daily return of \SI{49.5}{\bps} (Newey--West $t=11.06$) over the full sample. The economic and statistical magnitude collapses around NXT's launch: a one--percentage--point increase in NXT's share of total daily volume is associated with a \SI{6.4}{\bps} decline in the strategy's daily return ($t=-2.89$,
$R^{2}=0.024$), and the regression-implied break-even share, at which the strategy's expected daily return is zero, is approximately \SI{11.8}{\percent}---a threshold the data have now crossed. The attenuation is robust to point-in-time universe construction, a $5\times5$ grid of transaction-cost assumptions, the inclusion of
forcibly delisted firms, two-factor (market and size) alpha regressions, and a Chow/sup-$F$ structural-break test. We interpret these findings as evidence that the overnight reversal anomaly in Korea was sustained by the absence of independent premarket price discovery, and that NXT's entry attenuated the very informational friction the strategy was monetizing. The Korean experience differs systematically from the U.S.\ dark-pool environment along three institutional dimensions, which we identify and discuss.

papers.title: Exploiting the Overnight Market Anomaly in Indian Markets: Can Excess Returns Survive Market Frictions
papers.abstract: This study examines the practical exploitability of the overnight market anomaly in Indian equity markets using index futures. While prior research [4][12] suggests that most equity returns are generated outside trading hours, the economic viability remains uncertain once transaction costs, slippage, and taxes are accounted for. Using the past six-year historical data of the NIFTY future contracts to backtest a systematic trading strategy that maintains long exposure exclusively during overnight periods, entering positions near the market close and exiting them at the subsequent market open. The analysis incorporates realistic assumptions surrounding leverage, margin requirements, transaction costs [9], slippage, and statutory charges in the Indian derivatives market. The performance of the strategy is evaluated relative to a passive buy-and-hold exposure to the NIFTY Index and assessed using cumulative returns, volatility, Sharpe ratio [11], maximum drawdown [8], and risk-adjusted performance measures. The result provides evidence on the extent to which overnight returns contribute to the Indian equity market and whether this strategy can survive realistic market friction. The study further describes the practical challenges in converting a documented anomaly into an investment strategy

papers.title: Dark Side of the Day: Overnight Price Jumps and Short-Term Return Predictability
papers.authors: Hulusi Bahcivan, Lammertjan Dam, Halit Gonenc

papers.title: Dark Side of the Day: Overnight Price Jumps and Short-Term Return Predictability
papers.authors: Hulusi Bahcivan, Lammertjan Dam, Halit Gonenc

papers.title: News Sentiment and Overnight Return Prediction: Aid or Redundancy? Evidence from a Large Language Model
Heterogeneity in Overnight-versus-Intraday Stock-Return Behavior with Asymmetric Information and 52-week Price Anchoring
papers.authors: Chen Chen, Chris T. Stivers, Licheng Sun
papers.abstract: We document substantial cross-sectional heterogeneity in the overnight-intraday return anomaly along two distinct dimensions. First, a stock's asymmetric-information environment, summarized by our composite information-asymmetry metric (INFO-Z), predicts how last month's overnight return is propagated into this month's overnight and intraday returns. Higher INFO-Z stocks exhibit stronger overnight momentum and a stronger intraday cross-reversal. Second, a stock's price relative to its 52-week history, summarized by a composite price-to-52-week-anchor metric (PTA), predicts how last month's intraday return is propagated forward. High PTA stocks exhibit weaker intraday momentum and a weaker overnight cross-reversal. Stocks that were past relative winners are more important in establishing these conditional patterns. Our findings are robust across portfolio sorts, Fama-MacBeth regressions, and control variables motivated by recent explanations, and are stronger with higher investor sentiment. Our INFO-Z results complement the overnight-versus-intraday literature that emphasizes differentially informed agents. Our PTA results introduce the empirical importance of price anchoring in this setting and are consistent with an extrapolative-belief role. Finally, higher INFO-Z stocks earn higher average overnight returns and lower average intraday returns, highlighting the time-of-day dimension of information asymmetry.

papers.title: The Overnight Return Puzzle and the 'T+1' Trading Rule in Chinese Stock Markets
Are Return seasonality Due to Risk or Mispricing? Evidence from Anomaly seasonality
papers.abstract: This paper reexamines return seasonality in anomaly portfolios. While prior studies interpret anomaly and industry seasonality as explaining seasonality in individual stock returns, I show that interpreting anomaly seasonality as seasonality of risk premiums is misleading. Instead, it is mechanically inherited from stock-level seasonality through characteristic-based portfolio construction. Using 125 anomaly long-short portfolios and 1,238 corresponding raw portfolios, I find significant seasonality at annual lags in anomaly returns. However, anomaly-based seasonality fails to price seasonality strategies in individual stocks, whereas a seasonality factor constructed from individual stocks fully spans seasonality in anomaly portfolios. This asymmetric spanning relationship implies that anomaly portfolio seasonality is a projection of seasonality of individual stocks.

papers.title: Low-Risk Anomaly: Idiosyncratic Risk or Return Distribution
papers.authors: daye li, Tianyang Li, Honglin Xiong, Zhipeng Zhang

papers.title: The Predictable Tail: Lottery Characteristics Price Drawdown, Not Return -A Look-Ahead-Clean Audit in Which a Dissolving Return Anomaly Reappears as a Robust Risk Factor
papers.abstract: On a single point-in-time U.S. equity panel (715 names, 2009–2025) we document a sharp asymmetry: the cross-section of forward returns is barely predictable, while the cross-section of forward drawdowns is strongly predictable — by the same characteristics, on the same data. Total volatility has a rank information coefficient of ( , insignificant) against the forward 60-day return and ( ) against the realized 252-day maximum drawdown — a sixtyfold difference in predictive content for one variable. Lottery characteristics (payoff asymmetry, idiosyncratic skewness, MAX) show the same inversion at roughly fivefold. We organize the paper as four acts. Act 1 (the dissolving return anomaly): we take payoff asymmetry (PA) as a representative distributional signal and trace its apparent return premium through five separable artifacts — look-ahead contamination, mean-versus-rank divergence under fat tails, overlapping- window dependence, circular ex-post conditioning, and a spurious overlapping control — to a volatility-conditional residue that then fails a sector control, reversing within technology and carried by a single sub-period; the return signal is, at root, a healthcarecomposition effect. Act 2 (the inversion): repointed at realized drawdown, those same characteristics predict ruin robustly. Quality (high = safe) and the lottery axis (high skew/PA = fragile) survive an autocorrelation-corrected horserace against the volatility zoo and a Bonferroni correction across all trials ( down to ); the effect is out-of-sample stable and, for quality, strengthens in crises. Act 3 (why standard tooling misses it): on fat-tailed drawdown labels the Sharpe-based Deflated Sharpe Ratio reads while distribution-free gates (median NeweyWest, horserace, a Probability of Backtest Overfitting of ) are overwhelmingly significant — mean-Sharpe multiple-testing is the wrong instrument for a fat-tailed target — and we exhibit a momentum "ruin signal" that is pure overlap leakage, vanishing under a proper embargo. Act 4 (economic magnitude): the risk finding is not merely statistical — fragility-quintile membership separates the out-of-sample one-year probability of a drawdown from 4% to 44%, an actionable spread of a kind the return sort never produces. Throughout we use, and contribute, an adversarial validation gauntlet (look-ahead-clean construction, distribution-free inference, factor horserace, purged out-of-sample folds, multiple-testing penalties, and a continuousevaluation decay loop) whose job is to falsify its author's findings. The unifying message reframes the lottery literature: these characteristics are weak and fragile as return anomalies but strong, robust, and economically large as risk factors — and under fat tails, methodology fixes not just the magnitude but the sign of what one measures.

papers.title: A Return Prediction-Based Investment with Particle Filtering and Anomaly Detection
papers.authors: Masafumi Nakano, Akihiko Takahashi, Soichiro Takahashi

papers.title: Which Factors Macroeconomics or Financial More Influence Initial Return Anomaly in the Capital Market? Empirical Proving of WIPO Theory
papers.abstract: Various factors that influence investors’ decision in an IPO are reflected in the initial return anomaly. This paper analyse which factors are more influencing, financial, non-financial and macroeconomic, including stock-market performance on initial return. The research was conducted on 100 issuers in the IDX for the period 2018-2019 using the SEM method. The research shows that financial factors as systematic components have not a significant effect, but random components in the form of non-financial, macroeconomic, and stock market performance affect initial return. This result empirically proves WIPO theory and has important implications for market players, including the governments as the regulator.

papers.title: VIX1D with overnight weighting
Cross-Sectional Topological Anomaly Scores and Intraday Return Predictability in the S&P 500: A Ballmapper, Decoder-Conditional VAE, and Function-on-Function Regression Approach
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection methods in financial time series score statistically unusual observations in observable data, not topologically misexpected persistent deviations in the latent structure of comovement. This study constructs a stock-level topological anomaly score jointly conditioned on market-level topological structure and cross-sectional peer context, and tests whether its history carries predictive content for return curves. Intraday data for ten liquid S&P 500 constituents (April 2025-March 2026) are embedded via Takens delay embedding, graphed by BallMapper, and scored by three decoder-conditional variational autoencoder variants. Predictive content is assessed by penalised function-on-function regression and confirmed across all assets, intraday bar frequencies, and scoring variants, revealing a consistent temporal fingerprint-gradual accumulation of return impact, a frequent early reversal of its direction, and broadly distributed predictive content weighted toward recent anomaly history. When the reversal occurs depends on market regime; how evenly the anomaly history contributes to prediction depends on bar frequency.

papers.title: When Does Overnight Price Discovery Occur?
papers.abstract: This paper decomposes U.S. overnight stock returns into after-market, dark and pre-market components using one-minute transaction data for S&P 500 stocks. The explanatory power of intranight returns for final close-to-open returns rises gradually throughout the pre-market rather than jumping when foreign-market information becomes tradable in the U.S. pre-market or only when regular trading begins. Dark returns are positive on average, while pre-market returns are negative and partially reverse the dark return. The reversal is strongest when pre-market liquidity is lowest, consistent with an early illiquidity premium that declines as trading deepens. Early price movements are informative but not fully permanent.

papers.title: Overnight Corporate Bond Trading
papers.authors: Farshid Abdi, Marco Rossi, Botao Wu
papers.abstract: Corporate bond trades executed between 6:30 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. (ET) are not publicly disseminated until after TRACE reopens, generally between 8:00 and 8:15 a.m., creating a recurring interval of delayed post-trade transparency. Using enhanced TRACE data, we study how this temporary opacity affects trading and price discovery in the corporate bond market. Overnight trades are substantially larger than intraday trades and contribute disproportionately to price discovery. Overnight order imbalances predict future returns for both the same bond and other bonds issued by the same firm, indicating that overnight trades contain issuer-level private information. The price impact of overnight trades is significantly stronger and more persistent than that of intraday trades. Overnight activity is also more concentrated among large dealers and associated with higher dealer spreads and worse receiver outcomes. Finally, TRACE dissemination expansions increase overnight trading activity, suggesting that informed traders strategically shift trading toward periods with delayed disclosure.

papers.title: Trading-through Extended and Overnight Hours
papers.abstract: A common argument for lighter regulation is that competition makes mandatory rules unnecessary. In the context of retail trading, we test this directly by placing roughly 32,000 marketable orders across three brokers during the extended and overnight sessions, a natural laboratory where the order protection rule does not apply. Our trades average price dis-improvement at every broker, driven by pervasive and economically significant trade-throughs. This dis-improvement concentrates off-exchange: it is minimal when offexchange execution is largely inactive, and worsens when one broker moves its routing off-exchange. Our results speak directly to the value of order-protection and disclosure rules.

papers.title: Price Pressure and Overnight Seasoned Equity Offerings
papers.abstract: Between 2009 and 2014, 75% of seasoned equity offerings (SEOs) were announced and issued overnight, compared to 27% between 2000 and 2008. Overnight issuers obtain a higher SEO offer price because they experience more favorable pre-offer returns. Consistent with these favorable returns being due to the avoidance of pre-issue selling pressure, non-overnight issuers experience a 2.5% pre-issue stock price decline that reverses within seven days. This post-issue reversal is increasing in SEO offer size and bigger following large pre-issue price declines. In contrast, the returns following overnight offerings are less positive and unrelated to SEO offer size or pre-issue returns.

papers.title: Overnight Information and Anomalies
papers.authors: Jun Xie, Wenqian Xia, Bin Gao

papers.title: Risk-Based Overnight-Linked Futures Design
papers.abstract: The importance of overnight rate benchmarks has been increasing in the last years and is expected to increase further in the coming years. They could take over the IBOR-like benchmarks as the most important interest rate benchmarks. In this note we propose a new design for an overnight-linked futures. The design borrows on a swap futures design previously proposed by the author. The proposed design creates a potential unified approach to many interest rate futures and contributes to a common language between OTC and ETD markets. The design also reduces some of the drawbacks in existing futures.

papers.title: Overnight Returns, Limited Attention, and Labor Productivity
Overnight Returns, Limited Attention, and Labor Productivity
Overnight Returns, Daytime Reversals, and Anchoring Bias
From Breakouts and Momentum to Short-Term Reversal Sequential Strategy Development and Out-of-Sample Validation in U.S. Mid-Cap Equities
papers.abstract: This paper documents the sequential development and validation of three rule-based, long-only strategies in U.S. mid-cap equities under a common capital, timing, risk, and execution framework. The Legacy Breakout/Pullback strategy performed poorly, producing 65 trades and a total return of-47.0962%. Momentum52 represented a substantive redesign toward cross-sectional momentum, but its original later holdout failed: 54 trades returned-34.1037% with a profit factor of 0.5985. Reversal5 then shifted the economic premise toward short-horizon relative reversal conditioned on a positive longer-term stock trend. The final 7.5% trailing-activation specification produced 368 trades, a descriptive full-sample return of +70.5363%, an 11.2874% CAGR, and a profit factor of 1.2543. However, the 7.5% threshold was selected using development evidence, and the later historical segment was already inspected; that rerun is therefore confirmation rather than pristine out-of-sample parameterselection evidence. Over the harmonized 30 July 2025-10 September 2026 comparison window, Reversal5 returned +6.2405%, materially outperforming the two preceding project strategies but underperforming the raw-price, dividend-excluding MDY benchmark return of +15.6469%. The paper's principal contribution is thus both empirical and methodological: failed strategy generations remain visible, evidence classes are separated, and implementation assumptions are governed rather than retrospectively rewritten. The results are not survivor-bias-free because present-day S&P MidCap 400 constituents are projected backward, and they remain subject to raw-price corporate-action sensitivity, simplified trading costs, daily-bar path ambiguity, and portfolio concentration. Reversal5 is therefore the strongest historical specification in this governed strategy lineage, not evidence of a universal anomaly or demonstrated live alpha; genuinely prospective frozen signals are the critical next validation step.

papers.title: Short-Term Correlated Stress Reversal Trading
papers.abstract: Integrated Cross-Asset Stress Detection: We introduce an innovative methodology that leverages contemporaneous signals across diverse asset classes. By incorporating declines in risk assets (equities and commodities) alongside rallies in safe-haven instruments (U.S. Treasuries), our model robustly diagnoses market stress events that would otherwise be overlooked in a single-market framework.

papers.title: Short-Term Basis Reversal
papers.authors: Alberto G. Rossi, Yingguang Zhang, Yandi Zhu

papers.title: Short-Term Reversal Persists Globally-If Properly Measured
papers.abstract: Short-term reversal appears to have weakened in international equity markets because standard measures mix firm-specific and industry-wide returns. When evaluated relative to industry peers, the reversal persists. Using data from 64 countries, the conventional strategy delivers negligible returns, whereas an industry-adjusted strategy earns 0.53% per month with a Sharpe ratio of 0.74. The effect reflects the reversal of firm-specific shocks masked by persistent industry components. A regret-based signal captures the same industry-relative variation and adds no independent return. Reversal did not disappear; it was mismeasured.

papers.title: A Behavioral Look on Short-term Reversal
papers.authors: Bin Guo, Shen Lin, Wei Zhang
papers.abstract: Previous studies regard short-term reversal as compensation for liquidity risk. In this paper, we document that the reversal pattern depends on the prior realized profits that affect the risk attitude of the liquidity supplier. In the gain domain, a realized gain reduces the pain from a potential loss, making the liquidity supplier more risk-seeking. In the loss domain, a small realized loss motivates the break-even effect, but a substantial loss is too difficult to cover. Hence, there is an approximately U-shaped relation between the risk aversion of the liquidity supplier and realized loss. The empirical results confirm the asymmetric impacts of realized gain and loss on short-term reversal.

papers.title: Reversing the Trend of Short-Term Reversal
papers.authors: David Blitz, Bart van der Grient, Iman Honarvar
papers.abstract: The classic short-term reversal effect has steadily weakened over time, to the point of now having vanished entirely in most regions. However, the strategy can be revived by countering its tendency to go against short-term momentum in industry and factor returns. Enhanced short-term reversal strategies show a higher return with lower risk and have remained effective over time, culminating in more than double the risk-adjusted performance. Implementation challenges can best be overcome by combining short-term reversal with other short-term alpha signals. Various features of the short-term reversal strategy indicate that the premium stems from temporary imbalances between supply and demand. Investors in the strategy therefore effectively act as liquidity providers, contributing to a more efficient functioning of capital markets.

papers.title: Short-Term Reversal Profits and Dynamic Factor Exposures
papers.authors: David Blitz, Joop Huij, Simon Lansdorp, Marno Verbeek
papers.abstract: Conventional short-term reversal investment strategies exhibit dynamic exposures to the Fama-French factors. A reversal strategy based on residual stock returns does not exhibit these exposures and yields risk-adjusted profits that are twice as large as those of a strategy based on total stock returns. The residual reversal strategy also involves lower trading costs by being less concentrated in small-cap stocks. Our finding that residual reversal strategies generate economically large profits net of transactions costs in the large cap segment makes it difficult to attribute the reversal effect to trading frictions, liquidity, or nonsynchronous trading of stocks.

papers.title: Does the Short-Term Reversal Effect Challenge Market Efficiency?
papers.authors: David Blitz, Joop Huij, Simon Lansdorp, Marno Verbeek
papers.abstract: In this paper we analyze a short-term reversal strategy that is based on residual stock returns. While a reversal strategy that is based on total returns has time-varying exposures to common risk factors, this is not the case for a residual reversal strategy. We find that a residual reversal strategy has risk-adjusted profits that are twice as large as a total return strategy. Moreover, we find that a residual reversal strategy is profitable even after incorporating transaction costs. The findings of this study are at odds with the notion that markets are efficient.

papers.title: Short-term Reversal in Chinese A-Shares: Statistical Predictability, Economic Tradability, and Multiple Testing
papers.abstract: We study short-term reversal in Chinese A-shares on a fully traceable, point-in-time, delisting-inclusive database, using a monthly signal based on the past three months of returns that skips the most recent trading week. Over 2014:05-2026:02 (142 months), an equal-weighted loser-minus-winner long-short portfolio earns 1.72% per month (Newey-West 𝑡 = 3.64) and rises nearly monotonically across signal deciles (8 of 9 adjacent steps increasing). The effect is not absorbed by standard controls: a CH-3-style factor model leaves an alpha of 1.46% per month (𝑡 = 3.33), and Fama-MacBeth regressions controlling for size, earnings-to-price, Amihud illiquidity, and industry retain a significant reversal coefficient (𝑡 = 3.51). These risk-adjustment results survive multiple testing: under a Romano-Wolf step-down across the factor-model and Fama-MacBeth specification families, the featured specifications retain familywise-adjusted 𝑝-values of 0.0024 and 0.007, every one of the sixteen Fama-MacBeth specifications survives at adjusted 𝑝 ≤ 0.014, and all five factor-model specifications at 𝑝 ≤ 0.0032; the orthogonality also holds against the official Liu-Stambaugh-Yuan factors (alpha 1.88% per month, 𝑡 = 2.81, over the 2014-2021 overlap). Reversal is also not merely the volatility/lottery/turnover complex in disguise: when idiosyncratic volatility, the MAX lottery measure, turnover, beta, and momentum are measured over a window that does not overlap the signal-formation window, they leave the reversal coefficient intact (Fama-MacBeth 𝑡 = 4.3; three-factor alpha 1.32% per month, 𝑡 = 3.1). Such controls appear to absorb reversal only when measured over the same window as the signal-a mechanical artifact that vanishes monotonically as the control window is separated from it (§6.6). The tradable claim is weaker on every margin we examine. The long-only loser portfolio's excess over an equal-weighted universe is 0.25% per month (net-versus-net), loses single-test significance beyond 10-30 bps of proportional cost, and-measured against an investable cap-weighted index, the relevant opportunity cost-is economically large (about 1% per month) but statistically insignificant (𝑡 ≈ 1.5). After a max-𝑡 correction across 72 strategy-selection candidates the zero-cost excess is not significant (adjusted 𝑝 = 0.288), whether the long side is the loser half or the extreme loser decile. Returns concentrate in less-liquid small-and mid-cap stocks, and the long-short is materially lower in later subsamples (no formally identified trend). We read A-share short-term reversal as a genuine cross-sectional regularity-robust to standard factors and to a stock's pre-existing volatility/lottery/turnover character-that is nonetheless economically constrained as a trade: predictability and tradability diverge once multiplicity and frictions are treated explicitly.

papers.title: Short-Term Trading Strategy on G10 Currencies
papers.abstract:
This paper presents research on a profitable trading strategy for G10 currencies. We will devise trading strategies by considering realistic trading scenarios, analyze the performance of such strategies on out of sample data, identify the risks of these trading strategies, explain why the trading strategy works, and summarize and draw conclusions. We will use technical indicators like Moving average (MA), Exponentially-weighted moving average, Ichimoku, Relative strength index, stochastic oscillators, Williams %R, Commodity Channel Index, and Bollinger bands. We will also use fundamental indicators like interest rate differentials from one currency to another.

We will build a machine learning based model as it would be better equipped to build dynamic trading rules to capture profitable trading opportunities. We used an ensemble of machine learning algorithms - logistic regression with four principal components, and a voter classifier with random forest, extremely randomized trees, logistic regression with 4 principal components from the features, and support vector machine with 4 principal components from the features, giving 27% and 27% annualized returns, and 1.47 and 1.60 Sharpe ratio respectively.

papers.authors: Pasquale Della Corte, Robert Kosowski, Tianyu Wang

papers.title: Momentum and Reversal on the Short-Term Horizon: Evidence from Commodity Markets
papers.authors: Shen Zhao, Yiyi Ding, Jianfeng Yu, Wenjin Kang
papers.abstract: This paper documents the coexistence of momentum and reversal on the short-term horizon. Utilizing unique investors' position data from commodity futures markets, we decompose returns into a flow component tied to speculators' net trading (Q) and an orthogonal residual component (R nonQ). We find that R nonQ can significantly and positively predict next-week return (short-term return-based momentum), while Q forecasts nextweek return in a negative manner (short-term trading-based reversal). The short-term momentum effect applies to the entire cross-section of sample commodities and also to different subsamples of commodities with different characteristics. Further analysis shows that this short-term momentum primarily reflects speculators' trend-chasing trading behavior, which strengthens when volatility/uncertainty is low and when the expected profitability of momentum strategy is high. We also show that short-term momentum signals (R nonQ) can be aggregated to enhance the traditional intermediate-term momentum strategy and substantially improve its performance. By combining our empirical findings with a parsimonious model, we synthesize the microstructure-based liquidity-provision and behavioral trend-following mechanisms. Overall, our study demonstrates that momentum and reversal coexist on the same short-term horizon in commodity markets, overturns the previous canonical "reversal-at-short-horizon, momentum-at-intermediatehorizon" segmented perception, and therefore deepens our understanding about the overall return predictability in financial markets.

papers.title: Suspending Short-Term Rental Entry: The Portuguese Registration Ban and Its Reversal
papers.authors: Paulo Henrique Barbosa, Luiz Pinto Machado, Flávio Terto
papers.abstract: In October 2023 Portugal suspended new short-term rental registrations for apartments in covered mainland territory, exempting the interior, and reversed the suspension thirteen months later. The same law bundled a covered-territory levy with nationwide licensing rules. Using the universe of the national register, we estimate reduced-form entry effects from a triple difference across modality, statutory coverage and month, at the exact parish geography of the law. The package reduces apartment registrations in covered territory by 91 percent, an 89 percent differential net of national-average apartment movements, which we read as the response to the geographically targeted pair rather than a separation /of its instruments. Exempt-interior apartment entry falls by a fifth relative to detached houses and recovers when the nationwide rules are revoked. After the repeal the covered differential returns to within five percent of its pre-policy value, with equivalence bounded only within a quarter of a log point. The dynamics are consistent with the quantity restriction binding the legal entry margin, while the levy's independent entry effect is not identified.

papers.title: Competitive Incentives and the Persistence of Short-Term Value Destruction in Firm Strategy
Information Percolation, the 52-Week High, and Short-Term Reversal in Stock Returns
papers.authors: Zhaobo Zhu, Licheng Sun, Chris T. Stivers, Kai Zhang

papers.title: Model izbora optimalne kratkoročne strategije pivovare (An Optimal Short-Term Strategy Selection Model for a Brewery)
papers.abstract:
Croatian Abstract: Istraživanja pivarskoga sektora prepoznaju dva glavna endogena čimbenika koji utječu na potražnju neke marke industrijskoga piva: prodajnu cijenu te izdatak za marketing i ambalažu. No, dosadašnje su analize bile ograničene samo na pojedinačni utjecaj jednoga ili drugoga, uglavnom pritom koristeći neprimjeren model elastičnosti. Umjesto toga, ovaj rad predlaže dvodimenzionalnu sigmoidnu funkciju potražnje u obje varijable, koja je robusno prilagođena uvjetima promatranoga tržišta. S takvom funkcijom potražnje (podložnom ograničenjima tržišta i proizvodnoga kapaciteta) ugrađenom u financijski model društva, on postaje analitičko oruđe za maksimiziranje očekivane dobiti, tj. odabir optimalne kratkoročne strategije pivovare. Ovaj postupak ispitan je na modelu Zagrebačke pivovare, najvećega hrvatskog proizvođača piva, s obećavajućim rezultatima.

English Abstract: Research on the brewing sector identifies two major endogenous factors that impact demand for a certain industrial beer brand: the sales price and expenditure on marketing and packaging. However, prior analyses limited their scope to the individual impact of one or the other factor only, mostly using inadequate elasticity models. Instead, this paper proposes a two-dimensional sigmoid demand function in both variables, which is robustly adjusted to the conditions of the observed market. With such a demand function (subject to market and production capacity constraints) embedded into the company financial model, it becomes an analytical tool for the maximisation of expected profit, i.e. selection of the optimal short-term strategy for a brewery. This procedure has been tested on the model of Zagrebačka pivovara, the largest Croatian beer producer, with promising results.

papers.title: Drought avoidance strategy improves short-term hydraulic recovery from extreme drought for karst trees
papers.authors: Suhui Liao, Jiashuang Qin, Longkang Ni, Yu Tan, Daxing Gu
papers.abstract: Under the dual pressures of climate change and harsh terrain conditions, karst forests are expected to face increasingly frequent and severe droughts. Understanding how karst trees respond to extreme drought and subsequently recover their hydraulic functions is essential to elucidate the coordination between plant survival strategies under drought and their resilience to climate change.,Taking advantage of the extreme drought event that occurred in the Guilin region in 2022, we monitored the water potential, embolism levels, and hydraulic and structural traits of seven dominant tree species over a two-year period to characterize the hydraulic performance of karst trees during and after extreme drought and its correlation with water-related functional traits. Our results showed that the degree of embolism in the karst tree species at the end of extreme drought was influenced by the xylem water storage capacity, and the short-term hydraulic recovery capacity after extreme drought increased with the hydraulic safety margin of the shoot, which was determined mainly by isohydricity. Deep rooting traits coupled with strict stomatal regulation of isohydric plants formed a more conservative hydraulic regulation strategy, which promoted faster hydraulic recovery and represented a long-term strategy for the adaptation of karst trees to environmental fluctuations.,Our study demonstrated that drought avoidance traits in karst trees mitigated irreversible damage from water loss during extreme drought and improved short-term hydraulic recovery capacity.

papers.title: Intermediate-Term Reversal
papers.authors: Guan-Ying Huang, Kendro Vincent, Zong-Wei Yeh
papers.abstract: Long-term reversal is widely regarded as a fragile anomaly: the premium is concentrated in small and distressed firms and does not survive the standard risk adjustment. We ask whether this verdict reflects how the overreaction is measured rather than whether it occurs. Because the overreaction is an episode in the price path rather than a condition on its endpoints, we rank stocks on the maximum drawdown---the deepest peak-to-trough decline over a window that skips the most recent year---in place of the cumulative return. The sorts uncover an \textit{intermediate-term reversal} that sits between the momentum continuation and the classic long-horizon effect: the high-minus-low decile portfolio earns 1.16\% per month, with an eight-factor alpha of 0.87\% per month. Unlike the conventional strategy, the premium survives value weighting, persists among the stocks above the NYSE median capitalization, strengthens after 2000, and remains significant once the inference is corrected for the search across seventeen measurement horizons. It is not subsumed by momentum, the firm fundamentals, or a broad set of return predictors, and it concentrates in the stocks that are costly to arbitrage.

papers.title: Preventing Crashes: Enhanced Reversal Strategy in Chinese Stock Market
papers.authors: Fuwei Jiang, Geng Wang, Shuyu Xue
papers.abstract: In this paper, we find the stock returns of Chinese market exhibit reversal instead of momentum behavior from short to long horizons. While the traditional reversal strategies can generate economically large average returns in the Chinese market, they bear infrequently extreme downside risks. We hence propose enhanced reversal strategies by adding a stop-loss line to limit crash risk and constructing a composite reversal strategy to better select stocks. Our enhanced reversal strategy consistently provides stronger evidence of return reversal than does the traditional reversal strategy by doubling the Sharpe ratio, generating a vast monthly return of 1.75% and reducing the largest downside loss from -28.82% to -8.34%. The abnormal returns cannot be explained by the standard risk factor and are stronger among stocks with larger limits to arbitrage.

papers.title: Efficacy of a Mean Reversion Trading Strategy Using True Strength Index
papers.abstract:
This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of a mean reversion trading strategy, centered around the True Strength Index (TSI), applied to the SPY (S&P 500) and QQQ (Nasdaq Index) ETFs. The study spans historical data from 1996 to 2022, encompassing various market conditions to assess the strategy's robustness. The core methodology involves generating open and close signals based on the TSI, with supplementary insights from the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and other technical indicators.

Through rigorous backtesting, the paper evaluates key performance metrics such as Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR), Maximum Drawdown (Max DD), Sharpe Ratio, and Sortino Ratio. These metrics illuminate the strategy's profitability, risk management efficiency, and overall effectiveness. The strategy's adaptability is further demonstrated through a detailed walk-forward analysis, highlighting its performance over sequential three-year periods.

The paper aims to contribute to the financial market trading strategies literature, offering a nuanced understanding of the applicability and sustainability of mean reversion approaches in the dynamic landscape of equity markets. It offers a balanced view, discussing the strategy’s strengths, limitations, and broader implications for investors and traders. This research is significant for those seeking systematic methods to navigate the complexities of financial trading, underlining the importance of continuous adaptation and risk-awareness in investment practices.

papers.authors: Briac Turquet, Pierre Bajgrowicz, Olivier Scaillet

papers.title: Mean Reversion with Pair Trading in Indian Private Sector Banking Stocks
papers.abstract: While evaluating the performance of the company in the market, the stock performance of the company plays a vital role in its evaluation. In this paper, the correlation and mean reverting behaviour of various stocks of Banking (Private Banks) from Indian stock market have been examined. Five Private Sector Banks (ten combination/pairs among them) were selected for the study. Along with the correlation test, Augmented Dickey Fuller Test is conducted to test whether the time series follows the mean reverting behaviour. It has been found that three pairs from banking sector were negatively correlated and that high degree of correlation does not necessarily result in mean reversion between two time series.

papers.title: Speculative Futures Trading Under Mean Reversion
papers.authors: Tim Leung, Jiao Li, Xin Li, Zheng Wang
papers.abstract: This paper studies the problem of trading futures with transaction costs when the underlying spot price is mean-reverting. Specifically, we model the spot dynamics by the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU), Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR), or exponential Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (XOU) model. The futures term structure is derived and its connection to futures price dynamics is examined. For each futures contract, we describe the evolution of the roll yield, and compute explicitly the expected roll yield. For the futures trading problem, we incorporate the investor's timing option to enter or exit the market, as well as a chooser option to long or short a futures upon entry. This leads us to formulate and solve the corresponding optimal double stopping problems to determine the optimal trading strategies. Numerical results are presented to illustrate the optimal entry and exit boundaries under different models. We find that the option to choose between a long or short position induces the investor to delay market entry, as compared to the case where the investor pre-commits to go either long or short.

papers.title: Gold Silver Pair Trading -Mean Reversion Strategy Using Machine Learning
Optimal Mean Reversion Trading with Transaction Costs and Stop-Loss Exit
papers.abstract: Motivated by the industry practice of pairs trading, we study the optimal timing strategies for trading a mean-reverting price spread. An optimal double stopping problem is formulated to analyze the timing to start and subsequently liquidate the position subject to transaction costs. Modeling the price spread by an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, we apply a probabilistic methodology and rigorously derive the optimal price intervals for market entry and exit. As an extension, we incorporate a stop-loss constraint to limit the maximum loss. We show that the entry region is characterized by a bounded price interval that lies strictly above the stop-loss level. As for the exit timing, a higher stop-loss level always implies a lower optimal take-profit level. Both analytical and numerical results are provided to illustrate the dependence of timing strategies on model parameters such as transaction cost and stop-loss level.

papers.title: Short Term Trading Models – Mean Reversion Trading Strategies and the Black Swan Events
papers.authors: Mark Babayev, Folakemi Lotun, Goodwill Tatenda Mumvenge, Ritabrata Bhattacharyya
papers.abstract:
This research analyzed the effectiveness of Black Swan strategies for the Short-Term Mean-Reversion systems, the risks and rewards profiles of such betting systems based on the S&P500 index. In determining the Black Swan events, the research made use of multiple strategies against two portfolios. By utilizing the python notebooks, signals created by the Black Swan and Bollinger Bands trading strategies were compared for performance against the baseline index (buy-and-hold strategy). This was followed by a validation of how risk mitigation techniques like the stop-loss affect the trading performance. The research concluded that it is possible to construct a Mean-Reverse strategy that outperforms the market over time.
